title: Comparing two groups
bookRef: OpenIntro Statistics 4e, §6.2 (Difference of two proportions), §7.3 (Difference of two means)
audience: Adults who finished sessions s01-s07 of this course (center/spread, probability, normal model, standard error, confidence intervals, z tests, regression).
objectives: Estimate the difference between two proportions and its standard error.
Build and interpret a confidence interval for a difference of two proportions.
Test whether two proportions differ, using the pooled proportion under H0.
Explain when the difference of two means uses the t-distribution and why the groups must be independent.
keyIdeas: A difference of two independent estimates has variance equal to the sum of the variances.
SE of p̂1 − p̂2 = sqrt(p1(1−p1)/n1 + p2(1−p2)/n2); in a test of H0: p1 = p2 use the pooled p̂.
Randomised experiments allow causal conclusions; observational comparisons do not.
Paired data (before/after on the same people) are NOT two independent groups.
misconceptions: Subtracting the standard errors instead of adding the variances.
Concluding 'no difference' from overlapping individual confidence intervals.
Treating paired measurements as independent samples.
